again/loop: A language model writes text one token at a time: run the model on the sequence so far, pick the next token, append it, and run again.
again/redo: Done plainly, every step runs the whole sequence, so every block computes every token's key and value again, though only one token is new.
again/same: And the old ones come out the same every time. With the causal mask, an earlier token never attends to a later one, so adding a token changes nothing before it.
again/count: Count the keys. Step one computes one, step two computes two, and step ten computes ten: one plus two, and so on up to ten.
again/pair: To add that up, pair the ends. One plus ten is eleven, two plus nine is eleven, and so on to five plus six. Five pairs of eleven: fifty-five.
again/formula: Over T steps, there are T over two pairs, each adding to T plus one: T times T plus one, over two. For a thousand steps, five hundred times one thousand and one: five hundred thousand, five hundred.
cache/keep: So keep them. The KV cache stores the keys and values of every token so far, in every block.
cache/step: Each step now computes a query, key and value for the newest token only, adds its key and value to the cache, and attends over everything stored.
cache/work: Ten steps compute ten keys instead of fifty-five. For a thousand tokens, a thousand instead of half a million.
cache/shape: In one block, at step t, the cached keys form a t by d array, one row per token so far, and the values another. Each grows by one row per step.
cache/stack: Every block keeps a cache of its own. Stack the key caches of four blocks, block first, and they make one array of shape four, by t, by d. The values make another.
cache/memory: The price is memory. This block holds seven tokens, with d at six: seven rows of six numbers for the keys, and as many for the values. Two times seven times six: eighty-four numbers.
cache/total: Four blocks hold four times that: three hundred thirty-six. In general, two, times the blocks, times T, times d numbers, for every sequence being written.
